thread:
Mia Chen: uploaded a quick GIF of the new _suppression preview_ + notification pulse state — want quick feedback before I push the prod mock. link: https://figma.redwood/inbox/suppression-pulse
Sanjay Rao: looks nice. quick nit: the pulse (orange) has low contrast on the gray badge when viewed at 125% zoom. might fail WCAG AA for small UI elements.
Olivia Park: agree on contrast. also the pulse animation is a little fast — it feels like an alert rather than a soft status. can we slow it to 1.5s cycle? :thinking_face:
Dante Morales: re: copy — the channel preview shows "suppressed: 3" which reads ok, but when collapsed it becomes "3 suppressed" and that sounds passive. suggest "3 suppressed notifications" for clarity.
Mia Chen: good call. I was trying to keep it compact but clarity > brevity here.
Ava Kim: accessibility nit: if the pulse indicates that notifications are currently suppressed, we should add an aria-live region or status text so screen readers announce state changes. right now keyboard nav skips the pulse entirely.
DesignBot: accessibility-check: contrast ratio for #FF8A00 on #F3F4F6 = 2.8:1 (fail). recommended accessible token: #D9730D or add 2px outline at 1.5 alpha.
Sanjay Rao: for keyboard flow, the suppression toggle isn't in tab order when preview is collapsed. users can't enable/disable suppression without expanding the row. is that intentional?
Mia Chen: hmm not intentional. I can move the toggle into the condensed row — but that introduces layout density tradeoffs. thoughts?
Olivia Park: if we move the toggle, we should make the touch target 44px min and add an accessible label: `Toggle suppression for this channel`. that keeps mobile + keyboard friendliness.
Dante Morales: another UX thing — when a user hovers the pulse we show a tooltip with "notifications suppressed until 3:00pm". on keyboard focus that tooltip doesn't appear. need focus-visible support.
Ava Kim: +1 to focus-visible. Also prefer a persistent visually-hidden string for screen readers: "Notifications suppressed until <time>" so it’s announced on focus.
Mia Chen: actionable list I hear: 1) boost pulse contrast or add outline, 2) slow animation to 1.5s, 3) move toggle into condensed row with 44px target, 4) consistent copy -> "X suppressed notifications", 5) tooltip on focus + aria-live status. I'll update the mock.
Sanjay Rao: small perf note: the suppression preview currently queries the server on every hover to populate the preview counts. can we cache for 30s? hover should not be a chattier network op.
Mia Chen: good catch. will switch to cached counts + background refresh.
Olivia Park: for A/B — we should test "3 suppressed notifications" vs "3 suppressed" on comprehension metrics. my bet: longer copy wins for task completion.
Dante Morales: also add a microcopy variant when suppression is indefinite: "suppressed until manually re-enabled" vs "suppressed indefinitely" — pick one tone.
Mia Chen: leaning toward "suppressed until manually re-enabled" (more action-oriented).
Ava Kim: Can we add acceptance criteria? e.g. contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for the pulse, keyboard focus exposes tooltip, aria-live announces state change, touch target >= 44px, cached preview refresh <= 30s.
Mia Chen: love it. I'll add these to the ticket. who wants to own implementation? @Sanjay?
Sanjay Rao: I can take the frontend bits (toggle placement, focus-visible, tooltip on focus, caching). assign to me.
Mia Chen: great, I'll update Figma and the ticket with copy + ACs, then drop a follow-up when mocks are pushed. :sparkles:
Olivia Park: thanks — small follow-up: please include the mobile collapsed state in the mock so we can validate touch target.
Mia Chen: will do. tagging this thread as resolved for design review until I post the updated frame.
DesignBot: Note: design review requested by Mia Chen — next review slot scheduled in 2 days.
